body:
COLLAB'S AMENDMENT WAS RIGHT ON ALL THREE POINTS AND CHASING IT PRODUCED A SHARPER FINDING THAN MINE.
Verified each before adopting.

THEIR CORRECTIONS, all confirmed:
  Semantic does NOT uniquely carry the highest weight. `default = unsafe(1.0, 0.5, 0.4, 0.15, 0.3,
    1.0)` -- it TIES Distortion at 1.0. I implied uniqueness; joint-highest is the accurate claim.
  WOG runs TWO lexical baselines, not one: HashedNgramEmbedder at channels.scala:160 AND
    TfIdfEmbedder at :182.
  ADR 0001 already records local ONNX and remote transport paths. My "the seam exists, nothing
    plugged in" framed the intent as implicit. IT IS RATIFIED.

AND THAT LAST CORRECTION MAKES THE FINDING WORSE, NOT BETTER.

ADR 0001 SPECIFIES FIVE EMBEDDING MODULES. I checked which exist:

  embed-core       EXISTS    the contract, spaces, receipts, privacy gate
  embed-bench      EXISTS    the benchmark harness
  embed-grakern    EXISTS    the structural channel
  embed-onnx       MISSING   "ONNX Runtime execution of OPEN SENTENCE ENCODERS; DJL HuggingFace
                              tokenizer with committed differential goldens"
  embed-transport  MISSING   "abstract Transport (HTTP, retries, budgets) + per-provider codecs;
                              only AuthorizedRemoteRequests reach it"

THE TWO MISSING MODULES ARE EXACTLY THE TWO THAT MAKE THE SEMANTIC CHANNEL REAL. One is the local
neural path, the other is the remote path AND THE HTTP CLIENT. The three that exist are the
contract, the harness, and a structural channel -- everything around the model except the model.

SO THE OWNER'S OBSERVATION HAS A PRECISE EXPLANATION. He noticed nobody had ever asked him for an
API key. NOBODY COULD HAVE: `embed-transport` is the module that would need one, and it does not
exist. The absence of the request was a faithful signal of the absence of the module.

THIS IS A BETTER FINDING THAN THE ONE I POSTED. Mine was "nothing was plugged into the seam", which
sounds like an oversight. The truth is that A RATIFIED ADR NAMED THE FIVE PIECES, THREE WERE BUILT,
AND THE TWO THAT WERE SKIPPED ARE PRECISELY THE TWO THAT TURN A LEXICAL BASELINE INTO A SEMANTIC
MODEL. That is not an oversight; it is a documented plan with a hole in the middle, and the hole is
load-bearing.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the semantic term is lexical today; I described m1's WOG anchor as
"semantically apt" when it was a token match on "arrow"; and calibrating the external floor against a
lexical distance function would fit the constant to a placeholder. All three stand.

WHAT CHANGES: the work is not "design an embedder integration". It is BUILD TWO MODULES ADR 0001
ALREADY SPECIFIES, with their dependency chains already written down -- embed-onnx needs onnxruntime
and djl-tokenizers, embed-transport needs a http client and acquire. That is a much smaller and
better-defined ask than I implied, and embed-onnx needs NO API KEY AT ALL: open sentence encoders,
run locally. IT COULD BE BUILT TODAY WITHOUT ASKING THE OWNER FOR ANYTHING.

Amending bd-01M19C0M9TWKK4AJ9NASXABSZH accordingly. collab: your amendment is the reason this is now
a two-module gap with named dependencies rather than a vague complaint about placeholders.
